title: The Great Gatsby
author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
description: Nick Carraway recounts the life of his wealthy neighbor Jay Gatsby, whose pursuit of Daisy Buchanan exposes the illusions and divisions of Jazz Age America.

title: The Prince
author: Niccolò Machiavelli
description: A political treatise examining how rulers acquire and maintain power, often by balancing practical necessity against conventional morality.

title: Band of Brothers
author: Stephen E. Ambrose
description: An account of Easy Company, 506th Parachute Infantry Regiment, following its soldiers from training through their World War II campaigns in Europe.

title: The Republic
author: Plato
description: Through dialogues led by Socrates, Plato explores justice, the organization of an ideal state, and the relationship between knowledge and good government.

title: The Wealth of Nations
author: Adam Smith
description: An investigation into how nations generate prosperity through specialization, exchange, and institutions, alongside critiques of mercantilism.

title: The Call of the Wild
author: Jack London
description: Buck, a domesticated dog stolen into service during the Klondike Gold Rush, adapts to harsh conditions and discovers his ancestral instincts.

title: Theodore Roosevelt Trilogy
author: Edmund Morris
description: A three-volume biography tracing Theodore Roosevelt's youth, presidency, and later life: The Rise of Theodore Roosevelt, Theodore Rex, and Colonel Roosevelt.

author: George Orwell
description: Winston Smith attempts to preserve independent thought and personal love in a society ruled through surveillance, historical revision, and political terror.

title: Brave New World
author: Aldous Huxley
description: A technologically managed society maintains stability through biological engineering, conditioning, and pleasure, raising questions about freedom and human fulfillment.

title: How to Win Friends and Influence People
author: Dale Carnegie
description: A practical guide to interpersonal relationships that emphasizes sincere appreciation, attentive listening, and understanding other people's perspectives.

title: Roman Honor
author: Carlin A. Barton
description: A study of ancient Roman emotional and moral life, examining how honor, public judgment, and competitive display shaped identity and behavior.

title: Catch-22
author: Joseph Heller
description: American bombardier John Yossarian struggles to escape combat while trapped in the contradictory rules and self-serving bureaucracy of World War II.

title: Slaughterhouse-Five
author: Kurt Vonnegut
description: Billy Pilgrim becomes unstuck in time in a fragmented narrative connecting his ordinary life, wartime captivity, and the destruction of Dresden.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
description: The conflicts surrounding a troubled father and his sons culminate in a murder case that becomes an exploration of belief, guilt, and human freedom.

title: The Sun Also Rises
author: Ernest Hemingway
description: Jake Barnes and a circle of expatriates travel through France and Spain, seeking meaning and connection amid the emotional damage left by World War I.

title: For Whom the Bell Tolls
author: Ernest Hemingway
description: An American volunteer joins Republican guerrillas during the Spanish Civil War to destroy a bridge, confronting the personal costs of political commitment.

title: Swiss Family Robinson
author: Johann David Wyss
description: A shipwrecked Swiss family builds a new life on an island using practical skills, cooperation, and knowledge of the natural world.

title: On the Road
author: Jack Kerouac
description: Sal Paradise travels across America with the impulsive Dean Moriarty in a loosely autobiographical exploration of movement, music, and unconventional living.

title: The Dharma Bums
author: Jack Kerouac
description: Writer Ray Smith explores Buddhist ideas, mountain climbing, poetry, and bohemian friendship while seeking a more liberated way of life.

title: The Iliad & The Odyssey
author: Homer (traditionally attributed)
description: Two Greek epics recount Achilles' anger during the Trojan War and Odysseus' difficult journey home, exploring mortality, loyalty, and human struggle.

title: Walden
author: Henry David Thoreau
description: Thoreau reflects on his experiment living near Walden Pond, questioning material excess and exploring attention, independence, and humanity's relationship with nature.

title: The Lord of the Flies
author: William Golding
description: Published as Lord of the Flies, this novel follows stranded schoolboys whose attempts at self-government collapse into rivalry and violence.

title: Atlas Shrugged
author: Ayn Rand
description: As an industrial society deteriorates and leading innovators disappear, railroad executive Dagny Taggart investigates a mystery that dramatizes Rand's philosophy of Objectivism.

title: The Boy Scout Handbook (1st Edition)
author: Boy Scouts of America
description: An early American Scouting manual combining instruction in camping, first aid, woodcraft, and civic responsibility with guidance on character development.

title: Into Thin Air
author: Jon Krakauer
description: Krakauer recounts his experience of the 1996 Mount Everest disaster and examines the decisions, pressures, and conditions surrounding the tragedy.

title: King Solomon’s Mines
author: H. Rider Haggard
description: Allan Quatermain leads an expedition into southern Africa to find a missing man and the legendary diamond mines associated with King Solomon.

title: A River Runs Through It
author: Norman Maclean
description: The title novella of Maclean's collection connects fly-fishing in Montana with memories of family, particularly the bond between two very different brothers.

title: The Autobiography of Malcolm X
author: Malcolm X with Alex Haley
description: Malcolm X recounts his development from a troubled youth into an influential Black political and religious leader whose views continued to evolve.

title: The Count of Monte Cristo
author: Alexandre Dumas
description: Wrongfully imprisoned Edmond Dantès escapes, acquires a fortune, and adopts a new identity to punish those responsible for his downfall.

title: All Quiet on the Western Front
author: Erich Maria Remarque
description: Young German soldier Paul Bäumer experiences the brutality of World War I and the widening gulf between front-line reality and civilian expectations.

title: Pride & Prejudice
author: Jane Austen
description: Elizabeth Bennet and Fitzwilliam Darcy confront their mistaken judgments of one another within a society shaped by inheritance, reputation, and marriage.

title: The Art of War
author: Sun Tzu (traditionally attributed)
description: An ancient Chinese military treatise emphasizing preparation, knowledge of opponents, deception, and achieving objectives while minimizing costly conflict.

title: Lives
author: Plutarch
description: Also known as Parallel Lives, this collection pairs biographies of Greek and Roman figures to examine their characters, achievements, and moral failings.

title: The Bible
author: Various authors
description: A collection of sacred writings encompassing narrative, law, poetry, prophecy, letters, and wisdom; its contents vary among Jewish and Christian traditions.

title: Lonesome Dove
author: Larry McMurtry
description: Two former Texas Rangers lead a cattle drive to Montana, encountering danger, old attachments, and the limits of their frontier dreams.

title: After Virtue
author: Alasdair MacIntyre
description: MacIntyre critiques modern moral disagreement and argues for recovering an account of virtue grounded in practices, traditions, and shared human purposes.

title: The Maltese Falcon
author: Dashiell Hammett
description: Private detective Sam Spade becomes entangled with criminals and competing stories while investigating murders connected to a valuable jeweled statuette.

title: To Kill A Mockingbird
author: Harper Lee
description: Scout Finch observes prejudice and courage in an Alabama town as her father, Atticus, defends a Black man falsely accused of rape.

title: The Killer Angels
author: Michael Shaara
description: A fictionalized account of the Gettysburg campaign presents the battle through the perspectives of key Union and Confederate officers.

title: The Autobiography of Benjamin Franklin
author: Benjamin Franklin
description: Franklin recounts portions of his life and career while explaining his efforts to cultivate useful habits, moral character, and public service.

title: The Histories
author: Herodotus
description: An investigation into the conflicts between Greeks and Persians, interwoven with accounts of the customs, geography, and traditions of many peoples.

title: From Here to Eternity
author: James Jones
description: American soldiers stationed in Hawaii before Pearl Harbor navigate coercive hierarchies, personal loyalties, romantic entanglements, and the demands of army life.

title: The Thin Red Line
author: James Jones
description: An American infantry company fights on Guadalcanal, revealing how combat exposes individual fears, ambitions, and conflicting responses to violence.

title: Zen and the Art of Motorcycle Maintenance
author: Robert M. Pirsig
description: A motorcycle journey with the narrator's son becomes a framework for exploring quality, technical work, philosophical inquiry, and a fractured personal past.

title: The Long Goodbye
author: Raymond Chandler
description: Philip Marlowe's friendship with a troubled war veteran draws him into a murder investigation involving wealthy families, damaged relationships, and concealed motives.

title: Self-Reliance & Other Essays
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
description: Essays advocating independent judgment and trust in personal insight, with additional subjects varying by edition.

title: Ulysses
author: James Joyce
description: Following Leopold Bloom, Stephen Dedalus, and Molly Bloom through a Dublin day, Joyce transforms everyday experience through stylistic experimentation and Homeric parallels.

title: The Master and Margarita
author: Mikhail Bulgakov
description: The Devil's visit to Soviet Moscow intersects with a persecuted writer's love story and a parallel narrative about Pontius Pilate.

title: The Road
author: Cormac McCarthy
description: A father and son travel through a devastated landscape, struggling to survive without surrendering their remaining sense of humanity.

title: Steppenwolf
author: Hermann Hesse
description: Isolated intellectual Harry Haller confronts his fragmented identity through new relationships and surreal experiences that challenge his understanding of himself.

title: The Book of Deeds of Arms and Chivalry
author: Christine de Pizan
description: Also published as The Book of Deeds of Arms and of Chivalry, this work examines military practice, command, and the legal and ethical conduct of warfare.

title: Don Quixote
author: Miguel de Cervantes
description: An avid reader of chivalric romances reinvents himself as a knight and travels with Sancho Panza, repeatedly mistaking ordinary life for heroic adventure.

title: Invisible Man
author: Ralph Ellison
description: An unnamed Black narrator recounts experiences in the American South and Harlem while struggling against identities imposed on him by others.

title: The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn
author: Mark Twain
description: Huck Finn travels down the Mississippi River with Jim, an enslaved man seeking freedom, and confronts the contradictions of the society around them.

title: Leviathan
author: Thomas Hobbes
description: Hobbes argues that people establish a powerful sovereign to escape the insecurity of a condition without common political authority.

title: Nicomachean Ethics
author: Aristotle
description: Aristotle examines the good human life, arguing that flourishing depends on virtuous activity cultivated through habit, judgment, and relationships.

title: Cyrano de Bergerac
author: Edmond Rostand
description: A gifted swordsman and poet, insecure about his appearance, helps another man court the woman he secretly loves.

title: The Last Lion Trilogy
author: William Manchester; Paul Reid co-authored the third volume
description: A three-volume biography of Winston Churchill tracing his upbringing, political career, opposition to appeasement, and wartime leadership.

title: The Naked and the Dead
author: Norman Mailer
description: American soldiers fighting on a fictional Pacific island reveal the tensions between individual survival, military authority, and social hierarchy.

title: This Boy’s Life
author: Tobias Wolff
description: Wolff recalls an unsettled childhood with his mother and an abusive stepfather, examining the stories and ambitions through which he tried to remake himself.

title: Hatchet
author: Gary Paulsen
description: After surviving a plane crash in the Canadian wilderness, thirteen-year-old Brian Robeson must learn to obtain food, build shelter, and endure isolation.

title: Resilience
author: Eric Greitens
description: Interpreted as Resilience: Hard-Won Wisdom for Living a Better Life, a collection of letters drawing on philosophy and experience to discuss responding to hardship.

title: Tarzan of the Apes
author: Edgar Rice Burroughs
description: An English aristocrat's orphaned son grows up among apes in Africa and later encounters humans who challenge his understanding of his origins.

title: Thus Spoke Zarathustra
author: Friedrich Nietzsche
description: Through the teachings of the fictional prophet Zarathustra, Nietzsche explores humanity's possibilities after the decline of traditional religious and moral certainties.

title: The Federalist Papers
author: Alexander Hamilton, James Madison, and John Jay
description: A collection of eighty-five essays defending ratification of the United States Constitution and explaining the proposed federal government's structure.

title: The Godfather
author: Mario Puzo
description: The Corleone crime family navigates rivalries and succession as Michael Corleone becomes increasingly involved in the violent world he once resisted.

title: Moby Dick
author: Herman Melville
description: Published as Moby-Dick, this novel follows sailor Ishmael aboard the Pequod as Captain Ahab pursues the white whale that maimed him.

title: Frankenstein
author: Mary Shelley
description: Victor Frankenstein creates a living being but rejects it, setting in motion a tragedy shaped by abandonment, vengeance, and failed responsibility.

title: Hamlet
author: William Shakespeare
description: The prince of Denmark investigates his father's death and struggles to act against his uncle amid deception, grief, and a deteriorating royal court.

title: A Tale of Two Cities
author: Charles Dickens
description: Lives in London and Paris become entwined during the French Revolution in a story of political violence, family secrets, and redemptive sacrifice.

title: Revolutionary Road
author: Richard Yates
description: Frank and April Wheeler imagine escaping suburban dissatisfaction, but their conflicting desires and illusions place their marriage under growing strain.

title: The Divine Comedy
author: Dante Alighieri
description: Dante's imagined journey through Hell, Purgatory, and Paradise explores moral responsibility, political life, love, and the soul's movement toward God.

title: The Boys of Summer
author: Roger Kahn
description: Kahn recalls covering the Brooklyn Dodgers and revisits former players to examine their lives beyond baseball and the passage of time.

title: A Separate Peace
author: John Knowles
description: At a New England boarding school during World War II, Gene's relationship with his charismatic friend Finny becomes entangled with rivalry and guilt.

title: The Stranger
author: Albert Camus
description: An emotionally detached man in French-ruled Algeria commits a killing and faces a trial that judges both his crime and his refusal to follow social expectations.

title: Robinson Crusoe
author: Daniel Defoe
description: A shipwrecked sailor spends years building a life on an island, reflecting on faith, labor, isolation, and his encounters with others.

title: The 7 Habits of Highly Successful People
author: Stephen R. Covey
description: Interpreted as The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People, a guide to developing proactive habits, clear goals, effective relationships, and continuous renewal.

title: Cannery Row
author: John Steinbeck
description: An interconnected portrait of Monterey's waterfront residents centers on their eccentric relationships and a well-intentioned effort to honor a local marine biologist.

title: Treasure Island
author: Robert Louis Stevenson
description: Young Jim Hawkins joins a voyage to find buried treasure and discovers that the crew includes pirates led by the charismatic Long John Silver.

title: A Confederacy of Dunces
author: John Kennedy Toole
description: The grandiose and combative Ignatius J. Reilly moves through New Orleans, generating chaos as his lofty opinions collide with ordinary responsibilities.

title: Native Son
author: Richard Wright
description: Bigger Thomas, a young Black man in Chicago, becomes caught in a sequence of violence shaped by segregation, fear, and severely limited possibilities.

title: The Great Railway Bazaar
author: Paul Theroux
description: Theroux recounts a largely rail-based journey from Europe across Asia and back, focusing on fellow travelers, places, and the experience of movement.

title: The Last of the Mohicans
author: James Fenimore Cooper
description: During the French and Indian War, Hawkeye and his Mohican companions attempt to protect two sisters amid competing military and personal loyalties.

title: The Grapes of Wrath
author: John Steinbeck
description: The Joad family leaves Dust Bowl Oklahoma for California, where migrant labor conditions test their hopes, survival, and commitment to one another.

title: Education of a Wandering Man
author: Louis L'Amour
description: L'Amour reflects on the books, jobs, journeys, and encounters that shaped his education outside formal institutions and informed his writing.

title: Les Miserables
author: Victor Hugo
description: Former convict Jean Valjean seeks a moral new life while pursued by Inspector Javert against the backdrop of social conflict in nineteenth-century France.

title: Man’s Search for Meaning
author: Viktor E. Frankl
description: Frankl connects his experiences in Nazi concentration camps with logotherapy, an approach to psychotherapy centered on the human search for meaning.

title: The Outsiders
author: S. E. Hinton
description: Ponyboy Curtis navigates violent tensions between working-class Greasers and affluent Socs while struggling to understand identity, grief, and shared humanity.

title: One Hundred Years of Solitude
author: Gabriel García Márquez
description: Several generations of the Buendía family experience love, war, prosperity, and decline in the fictional town of Macondo.

title: Gates of Fire
author: Steven Pressfield
description: A fictional survivor recounts Spartan training and the stand at Thermopylae, exploring the relationships and beliefs that sustain warriors under extreme pressure.

title: Paradise Lost
author: John Milton
description: Milton retells Satan's rebellion and the fall of Adam and Eve in an epic examination of freedom, responsibility, and humanity's relationship with God.

title: Fahrenheit 451
author: Ray Bradbury
description: Guy Montag, a fireman employed to burn books, begins questioning a society that suppresses difficult ideas and discourages reflective thought.

title: Oil!
author: Upton Sinclair
description: The son of a California oil magnate becomes increasingly troubled by the exploitation and political influence surrounding his father's industry.

title: Fear and Trembling
author: Søren Kierkegaard
description: Writing as Johannes de Silentio, Kierkegaard examines Abraham's willingness to sacrifice Isaac to explore the troubling relationship between faith and universal ethics.

title: The Code of Man
author: Waller R. Newell
description: Newell draws on Western literature and philosophy to argue for an ideal of manhood organized around love, courage, pride, family, and country.

title: Heart of Darkness
author: Joseph Conrad
description: Marlow recounts a journey into the Congo to find the ivory trader Kurtz, exposing colonial violence and the instability of claims to civilization.

title: Meditations
author: Marcus Aurelius
description: Private philosophical reflections by a Roman emperor explore how to govern one's judgments, fulfill responsibilities, and respond calmly to change and death.

title: The Hobbit & The Lord of the Rings
author: J. R. R. Tolkien
description: Connected adventures in Middle-earth follow Bilbo Baggins' unexpected quest and the later struggle to destroy the One Ring and defeat Sauron.

title: With the Old Breed
author: E. B. Sledge
description: Sledge recounts his experiences as a U.S. Marine at Peleliu and Okinawa, emphasizing the physical horror and psychological strain of Pacific combat.

title: Self-Control: Its Kingship and Majesty
author: William George Jordan
description: A collection of essays presenting mastery of impulses, thoughtful conduct, and inner steadiness as foundations of a constructive life.

title: The Abventures of Tom Sawyer
author: Mark Twain
description: Interpreted as The Adventures of Tom Sawyer, a story of a mischievous boy whose escapades along the Mississippi lead to danger and growing responsibility.

title: The Idiot
author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
description: The candid and compassionate Prince Myshkin enters Russian high society, where his goodness becomes entangled with jealousy, desire, and social calculation.

title: The Collectied Jack London
author: Jack London
description: Interpreted as a collected edition of Jack London's writing; the exact contents and balance of novels, stories, or other works depend on the edition.
